recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Reintroducing entered-in-error on a legacy status element or duplicating guidance would conflict with the current split clinicalStatus/verificationStatus model; no core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5724.
issue_request: FHIR-5724 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request from DSTU1 asking to add an entered-in-error equivalent to AllergyIntolerance.status and Condition.status because similar resources consistently had one.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in git-svn commit b9fb8b6f13 (svn revision 4843), which added entered-in-error to the then-current AllergyIntolerance.status and Condition.status spreadsheet definitions.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance and Condition are active current-build Patient Care resources. Later published Patient Care decisions changed the status model: FHIR-11151 split AllergyIntolerance.status into clinicalStatus and verificationStatus and aligned it with Condition; FHIR-11206 clarified entered-in-error is not an inactive clinical state; and FHIR-23008/FHIR-28458 adjusted invariants and guidance after verificationStatus became CodeableConcept. The current source therefore represents the old status request on verificationStatus rather than on a removed legacy status element.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current StructureDefinitions for both resources declare the build entered-in-error-status hook as .verificationStatus = entered-in-error, their verificationStatus short descriptions include entered-in-error, and their verification-status search parameters expose the code.
